slot.brief: Dimensional analysis: given a physics equation involving a new/defined quantity (e.g. coefficient of viscosity, Planck-like constant), find the dimensional formula of the unknown constant by dimensional homogeneity of all terms.

stem: A model for energy $E$ is written as $E=\eta v r^2+K\dfrac{\eta^2}{\rho}$, where $\eta$ is dynamic viscosity, $v$ is speed, $r$ is length and $\rho$ is mass density. What is the dimensional formula of $K$?

verdicts.working: Since [η]=[M L⁻¹ T⁻¹] and [ρ]=[M L⁻³], [η²/ρ]=[M L T⁻²]. Thus [K]=[E]/[η²/ρ]=[L].

working:
$[\eta]=[\text{M}\text{L}^{-1}\text{T}^{-1}]$, $[v]=[\text{L}\text{T}^{-1}]$, $[r]=[\text{L}]$. 
$[\eta v r^2]=[\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]=[E]$. 
$[\eta^2/\rho]=[\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-2}]$, hence $[K]=[E]/[\eta^2/\rho]=[\text{L}]$.

Independent check: Since [η]=[M L⁻¹ T⁻¹] and [ρ]=[M L⁻³], [η²/ρ]=[M L T⁻²]. Thus [K]=[E]/[η²/ρ]=[L].
